name: Nails
label: Southern Lord
lede: Todd Jones, guitarist of Terror, started a band whose songs mostly run under two minutes, and Kurt Ballou has recorded every album.

eras.title: A lifer with a Minor Threat CD
eras.text: Todd Jones came up in Oxnard's hardcore scene, then spent years as a guitarist for other people's bands. Nails is what he did when he decided to stop waiting for a band that sounded like what he wanted to hear.

years.h: Todd Jones plays his first bands in Oxnard, including It Doesn't Matter
years.p: Jones says his first show was around New Year's 1995 or 1996 with It Doesn't Matter, which appeared on the 1996 compilation Localism. He also played in Betrayed, Internal Affairs and FireBurn.
years.xp:
Jones told No Echo that a friend's borrowed Minor Threat CD hit him at about 13 or 14: he had been waiting his whole life to hear it.

Before Nails he was the guitarist in the Revelation-inspired straight-edge band Carry On, then in [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]] alongside Scott Vogel.

years.h: Todd Jones takes the guitar spot in [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]]
years.p: After Carry On ended, Jones joined Scott Vogel in Terror, the Los Angeles band rooted in New York hardcore. That job made him a name, and it is where Nails begins.

eras.title: Two minutes, no filler
eras.text: Nails start in December 2007 with Jones, drummer Taylor Young and bassist John Gianelli. They play short, brutal songs, and they land at Kurt Ballou's studio in Salem, Massachusetts.

years.cap: Nails, early shows in Southern California
years.h: Nails form in Oxnard from Terror's Todd Jones
years.p: Southern Lord dates the band to December 2007: Jones, drummer [[Taylor Young|b819904a-345d-4cc9-95b9-ee0bf9b3c3d2]] and bassist John Gianelli. Jones has said he began Nails because he wanted to do what he wanted rather than join a group and negotiate a style.
years.xp:
Jones had taken a break from music, and told No Echo he was simply not in a band for a while. Nails was his way back, built on his own taste: crust, death metal and Japanese hardcore, with Agnostic Front, Discharge, Slayer and Sheer Terror among the names he cites.

Southern Lord later described the sound as the good AmRep bands of the nineties plus Cro-Mags Age of Quarrel riffs at breakneck speed.

years.h: Obscene Humanity is the first Nails record
years.p: A short 12-inch that introduces the Nails sound before any full-length. The 2020 reissue of Unsilent Death later added three of its tracks.
Recorded December 27, 2009 to January 2, 2010 with Kurt Ballou at God City in Salem. The CD came out via Six Feet Under, and Jones released the vinyl himself on his Streetcleaner label.
years.xp:
Wikipedia gives the release as March 12, 2010 and the length as 13 minutes 52 seconds. Ballou engineered and mixed it, starting a working relationship that lasted through every Nails album.

Southern Lord later reissued it, including a 10th anniversary edition.

years.h: Kurt Ballou becomes the sound of Nails
years.p: Jones told Heavy Blog Is Heavy that Ballou is opinionated and smart, and that he knows how to record an HM2 pedal, the buzzsaw guitar distortion behind the Nails tone.

eras.title: Southern Lord takes them on
eras.text: Nails move to a proper heavy-music label and sharpen up. Abandon All Life is the record where the band's reputation stops being an underground rumor.

years.h: Split with Skin Like Iron and a 7-inch of Obscene Humanity
years.p: Nails share a 7-inch with Skin Like Iron in 2012, and Obscene Humanity gets a 7-inch pressing the same year.
Released March 28, 2013, recorded over the New Year at God City with Kurt Ballou; the longest song is the five-minute-plus Suum Cuique. It runs 17 minutes 14 seconds.
years.xp:
Recording ran December 27, 2012 to January 2, 2013. Brad Boatright mastered it and Andy Saba played session lead guitar. Metacritic lists 80/100, with 8.0 from Pitchfork.

Jones later told Heavy Blog Is Heavy the album felt aggressive but not memorable: you feel beaten up, but do not remember much of the beating.

years.h: Jones limits Nails to a few weeks of touring a year
years.p: Todd Jones has kept a day job and says he tours Nails four to six weeks a year. He chooses that because of things in life he would otherwise give up.
years.xp: In the CVLT Nation interview Jones says he is not a full-time touring musician by choice, and that his coworkers would likely not understand grindcore if they found out.

eras.title: Longer, thicker, and a big label
eras.text: For the third album Jones wanted the extremity of Abandon All Life joined to the catchiness of Unsilent Death. It is Nails' biggest release, and then the band goes quiet in an odd way.

years.h: You Will Never Be One of Us on Nuclear Blast
years.p: Released June 17, 2016, it runs 21 minutes 43 seconds, with the eight-minute-plus They Come Crawling Back. It peaked at number 127 on the Billboard 200, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
Recorded December 27, 2015 to January 6, 2016 with Kurt Ballou at God City. LA Weekly ranked it number one among its top metal albums of 2016, and it appeared on year-end lists in Rolling Stone, Metal Hammer and Metal Injection.

Jones described the aim to Heavy Blog Is Heavy as combining the extremity of Abandon All Life with the thickness of Unsilent Death.
play: You Will Never Be One of Us

years.h: A European tour is cancelled, and promoters say Nails are done
years.p: On July 25, 2016 the band cancelled its European tour, and promoters said the band was on hiatus with no plans to play or record. Jones said there had never been an official hiatus.
years.xp:
The cancellation also removed a spot on the Ozzfest Meets Knotfest bill. Nails were back on stage that December at The Power of the Riff festival and released a split 7-inch with Full of Hell.

No reason for the cancellation appears in the sources I found.

eras.title: Quiet, then a Cavalera
eras.text: Nails release less and play less. In 2019 the band puts out a 7-inch with Max Cavalera. In 2020 both original partners of Todd Jones leave.

years.h: I Don't Want to Know You 7-inch features Max Cavalera
years.p: The 2019 release has Sepultura and Soulfly founder [[Max Cavalera|5970bee1-1713-4970-be17-a801b863a273]] as a guest.

years.h: Drummer Taylor Young and bassist John Gianelli leave Nails
years.p: Young announced his exit in early spring 2020, and Gianelli confirmed his the next day, leaving Todd Jones as the only original member.
Released November 27, 2020 through Southern Lord with three Obscene Humanity songs and two previously unreleased songs from the original sessions.

eras.title: Every Bridge Burning
eras.text: After nearly three years of silence and an eight-year gap between albums, Jones rebuilds Nails and returns to Kurt Ballou.

years.h: Nails announce a new album, engineered by Kurt Ballou
years.p: The announcement came on Instagram and confirmed a Nuclear Blast release, recorded at God City with Ballou.
The fourth album has guitarist Shelby Lermo, drummer Carlos Cruz and bassist Andrew Solis. Singles were Imposing Will, Give Me the Painkiller and Lacking the Ability to Process Empathy.
years.xp:
Recorded October 2023 to January 2024. Jones says the record is about isolation and deteriorating friendships, and that a lot came out after Covid.

Lermo was in Ulthar, Cruz plays in Warbringer, and Solis in Despise You and Apparition.

years.p: Wikipedia lists a Fear Based Life 7-inch for 2026.
